post_mortem.why_failed: The revision added targeted downgrades that removed previously-high scoring cuts: the numeric+unit exception demoted splits like numeral↔unit (e.g., six / miles) and the name/org+subordinating rule demoted cuts around named organizations before subordinators (e.g., …Association / due …). By removing those safe/high-scoring boundaries the truncator had to keep worse alternatives that more often contradicted the full-sentence translation, dropping the measured objective.
blamed_lines: +- Numeric+unit split exception (traceable to en_us_66): Do NOT apply the generic numeral boost when the marker splits a numeric token from an immediately following unit/scale token. Concretely: if the token immediately before the marker is a numeral (a digit sequence or formatted number token) and the token immediately after the marker is one of {million, billion, thousand, percent, %, k, m, mi, kg, miles, signatures, signature, dollars}, then do NOT bias upward; instead bias the marker downward into a lower target band (0–40).

+- Name/organization + subordinating continuation exception: When the token immediately before the marker looks like a name or organization (a capitalized token or tokens ending with common org suffixes such as Inc, Corp, Ltd, LLC, or a short all-capital acronym) AND the token immediately after the marker is a subordinating continuation token in {due, because, to}, then reduce or remove the usual name/org boost and bias the marker downward into the lower target band (0–40).

+- Is the token immediately before the marker a numeral/date/percentage/name? If yes, bias score upward, except when a targeted exception above applies (numeric+unit, name/org + subordinating continuation). For numeric+unit splits, move the marker into band 0–40 instead of boosting.
post_mortem.lesson: Targeted downgrades must be narrowly scoped and not broadly remove previously-safe high-scoring cuts—test that exceptions only affect the exact token shapes intended (e.g., digit tokens vs spelled-out numbers) to avoid forcing worse kept boundaries.
